articles.title: Does deliberating on politics make you look weak or wise? New research weighs in
articles.summary: People who take time to deliberate before choosing a side on a political issue tend to be judged as having better moral character by those who disagree with them, according to new research.

articles.title: Strong social networks predict higher fertility rates in new study
articles.summary: Communities where people report high levels of social support and frequent social interactions tend to have higher birth rates, regardless of their economic status. This pattern suggests that strong social networks may help sustain regional populations.

articles.title: Eye contact may act as a learning “switch” for babies’ brains
articles.summary: Do babies soak up everything they hear? Not quite. A study of infants in the U.K. and Singapore suggests eye contact helps them decide which words are worth learning, possibly by syncing their brain activity with the speaker's.

articles.title: Brain replays motor skills during sleep without help from the memory center
articles.summary: During sleep, the brain replays the day's events to lock in memories. A new study reveals that the brain networks governing physical habits can run these offline rehearsals entirely on their own, challenging classic theories of memory.

articles.title: Frontiers: A Roundtable Discussion on the I-Frame vs. S-Frame Debate
articles.summary: Applied behavioral scientists believe their work can influence people’s lives for the better. But what is the most effective way to make that happen? Is it through interventions focused on influencing individual behavior while maintaining freedom of choice? Is it by changing policies and laws, and thereby the systems, that individuals operate within? Is it a combination of the two? Is the distinction between an individual- or systems-focus a helpful one? Or, is the world too messy and complex? How should applied behavioral scientists navigate the financial and political influences on the work

articles.title: Scientists say this simple habit could strengthen your marriage
articles.summary: Couples who exercise together report better communication, healthier conflict resolution, and lower marital stress than those who work out alone. Even something as simple as taking a walk together may create valuable opportunities to talk, listen, and feel more connected.

articles.title: What happens in the brain when cannabis makes you anxious?
articles.summary: Cannabinoids may intensify anxiety by removing a natural brake on specific neurons in the brain’s fear center, particularly during stressful situations. In mice, shutting down those neurons sharply reduced cannabinoid-related anxious behavior.

articles.title: Vagus Nerve Stimulation Could Help New Skills Stick
articles.summary: Stimulating the vagus nerve after practice helped mice develop stronger long-term motor learning, revealing a potentially important window when the brain is still locking in a new skill. The effect was linked to rhythmic changes in brain blood vessels, hinting that body-to-brain signals may help prepare the brain for lasting change.

articles.title: Adaptive Workflow Intelligence: A Cognitive Architecture for Context-Driven Enterprise Automation
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.08793v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Enterprise systems increasingly rely on automated workflows, yet many AI-driven solutions remain brittle under non-stationary conditions, evolving policies, and delayed operational feedback. While reinforcement learning and large language model (LLM) agents offer partial adaptability, they do not by themselves provide persistent reflection mechanisms or straightforward integration with policy-constrained enterprise operations. This paper introduces Adaptive Workflow Intelligence (AWI), a cognitive architecture for context-driven enterprise agents

While recent optimization-based SMT solvers have successfully applied gradient descent to continuous relaxations of logical formulas, they are fundamentally bottlenecked by gradient domination, a phenomenon where a small subset of difficult clauses hijacks the optimization trajectory, preventing the solver from satisfying the broader formula and trap

articles.summary: arXiv:2610.08814v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Compositional generalization remains challenging when language models must combine familiar reasoning operations in unfamiliar ways. articles.title: An Empirical Study of Agent Skills' Downstream Utility
articles.summary: arXiv:2610.08875v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Agent Skills package procedural guidance and resources for reuse, but a relevant Skill does not necessarily improve task performance.
